question: Find the weighted average of the numbers 17, 12, 23, 45, and 301, using the respective weights 29, 87, 15, 26, and 18.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the deviation method, assume a base weighted average of 12.

Net weighted deviation = ∑ [Weight × (Value − Base)]

Net deviation = 29×(17−12) + 87×(12−12) + 15×(23−12) + 26×(45−12) + 18×(301−12)

Net deviation = (29 × 5) + 0 + (15 × 11) + (26 × 33) + (18 × 289) = 145 + 0 + 165 + 858 + 5202 = 6370

Average deviation = 6370 ÷ (29 + 87 + 15 + 26 + 18) = 6370 ÷ 175 = 36.4

Weighted Average = Base + Average deviation = 12 + 36.4 = 48.4

**∴ The correct answer is 48.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers (X) = 17, 12, 23, 45, 301

Weights (W) = 29, 87, 15, 26, 18

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average = ∑(W × X) ÷ ∑W

 Weighted Average = Sum(Value × Weight) ÷ Total Weight
 ∴ 8470 ÷ 175 = 48.4

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of Weights (∑W) = 29 + 87 + 15 + 26 + 18

⇒ ∑W = 175

⇒ Sum of Products (∑(W × X)) = (29 × 17) + (87 × 12) + (15 × 23) + (26 × 45) + (18 × 301)

⇒ ∑(W × X) = 493 + 1044 + 345 + 1170 + 5418

⇒ ∑(W × X) = 8470

⇒ Weighted Average = 8470 ÷ 175

⇒ Weighted Average = 48.4

**∴ The correct answer is 48.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

It is a type of average where some data points contribute more heavily to the final value than others. Formula used is Aw = ∑(wᵢxᵢ) ÷ ∑wᵢ.

Arithmetic Mean

The standard mean calculated by adding up all the data values and dividing by the total number of items. It assumes all weights are strictly equal.

Combined Average

When two distinct groups of sizes n₁ and n₂ have individual averages A₁ and A₂ respectively, their overall combined average is represented as (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).
